summary: 把 pulls a known, specific object in front of the verb so the sentence can say what was done TO it: where it ended up, what state it is in now, who got it. So the verb can never stand bare after 把: something must follow it (a result, a direction, 了, 在/到/给 + destination, 一下). Think 'take X and do-something-to-completion'. No change to the object, no 把.

subs.label: 把 + object + verb + result
subs.focus: Learner must place the object between 把 and the verb and keep verb + result (完, 好, 坏, 干净, 上, 掉, 错) together, with 了 last. Errors: object left after the verb (我把喝完了咖啡), result split off, 把 before the subject. Rewrites go from SVO + result to 把 and back.

subs.label: 把 + object + verb + direction
subs.focus: 把 with directional complements (拿出来, 带回去, 搬进去, 拿走, 带来). Learner must keep the object before the verb and the whole direction after it. Errors: object inside or after the complement (把拿书出来, 把拿出来书), or dropping the direction so the verb is bare.

subs.label: Obligatory 把: 放在 / 送到 / 交给 / 翻译成 / 当作
subs.focus: Verb + 在 / 到 / 给 / 成 / 作 + place, person or new form, with a specific object: the object must go forward with 把. Force 把 over English order (我放书在桌子上, 他翻译这句话成中文) and test which of 在 / 到 / 给 / 成 fits the verb.

subs.label: No bare verb after 把
subs.focus: Minimal endings when there is no result or direction: 了 (with 吃, 喝, 卖, 扔, 忘, 丢, 脱), reduplication (擦一擦), 一下. Learner must reject a bare verb (我把作业做, 请把门关) and pick a fitting ending. Cloze should offer ∅ as the tempting wrong option.

subs.label: 没 / 别 / modals / adverbs go before 把
subs.focus: 没, 别, 不要, modals (可以, 能, 要, 想, 应该) and time adverbs (已经, 还没, 马上) go before 把, not between object and verb. Errors: 你把车可以停在这儿, 我把没作业做完. 把…没 + verb is said colloquially: never judge-wrong. Also test 没 (not 不, and no 了) for an action not done. Keep 把 and the negator or modal as separate tiles.

subs.label: Verbs that cannot take 把
subs.focus: Verbs that do nothing to the object take plain SVO: 是, 有, 在; 喜欢, 知道, 觉得, 认识; 来, 去, 到, 回; perception with only 见 / 到 (看见, 听到). Learner must reject 我把他喜欢, 我把他看见了. Mix in correct look-alikes for judge items (把字看清楚了, 把这件事忘了).

subs.label: The 把 object is specific
subs.focus: The 把 object is identifiable (这 / 那, 我的, pronoun, bare noun = 'the ...'); a new counted object (一本书, 两杯咖啡) stays after the verb. Learner chooses 把那本书看完了 or 看完了一本书 from the cue ('the / that / my' or 'a / some / two'). 把 + 一 + measure is accepted colloquially: never use it as a judge-wrong sentence.

subs.label: 把 or plain SVO?
subs.focus: Is 把 possible at all? Plain SVO for habits, ongoing actions and statements with no outcome (我每天喝咖啡), and for potential complements (做不完, 看得懂). Errors: 我把这些作业做不完, 我每天把咖啡喝. Definite object + result allows both orders: use rewrites, never judge one as wrong.

rules.rule: Put the specific object right after 把, then the verb with its result. Verb and result stay glued together; 了 comes after them.
rules.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Result + (了)

examples.py: wǒ bǎ zuò yè xiě wán le
examples.en: I've finished my homework.

examples.zh: 弟弟把我的手机弄坏了。
examples.py: dì di bǎ wǒ de shǒu jī nòng huài le
examples.en: My little brother broke my phone.

examples.py: qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng
examples.en: Please close the door.

examples.py: mā ma bǎ yī fu xǐ gān jìng le
examples.en: Mum washed the clothes clean.

rules.note: Requests and plans (请把门关上, 我想把房间打扫干净) have no 了 because nothing has happened yet.

rules.rule: With a direction after the verb (出来, 回去, 进去, 走, 下), the object goes before the verb with 把 and the whole direction follows the verb.
rules.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Direction + (了)

examples.py: qǐng bǎ shū ná chū lái
examples.en: Please take your books out.

examples.py: tā bǎ yǐ zi bān jìn qù le
examples.en: He carried the chair inside.

examples.py: nǐ bǎ sǎn dài huí qù ba
examples.en: Take the umbrella back with you.

examples.zh: 谁把我的自行车骑走了？
examples.py: shéi bǎ wǒ de zì xíng chē qí zǒu le
examples.en: Who rode off on my bike?

rules.note: Without 把, other orders exist (拿出一本书来), but once 把 is used the object can only be in front of the verb.

rules.rule: If the verb is followed by 在 / 到 + place, or has 给 + person attached to it, in standard Mandarin a specific object does not stay after the verb. Move it forward with 把.
rules.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + Place / Person

examples.zh: 我把手机放在桌子上了。
examples.py: wǒ bǎ shǒu jī fàng zài zhuō zi shàng le
examples.en: I put my phone on the table.

examples.zh: 司机把我们送到了机场。
examples.py: sī jī bǎ wǒ men sòng dào le jī chǎng
examples.en: The driver took us to the airport.

examples.zh: 请把这封信交给李老师。
examples.py: qǐng bǎ zhè fēng xìn jiāo gěi lǐ lǎo shī
examples.en: Please hand this letter to Teacher Li.

examples.zh: 你什么时候把书还给我？
examples.py: nǐ shén me shí hou bǎ shū huán gěi wǒ
examples.en: When are you giving the book back to me?

rules.note: 在 is for where the thing rests (放在, 写在, 挂在, 停在); 到 is for where it is moved to (送到, 搬到, 带到, 拿到). Giving verbs have other orders without 把 when the object is new or counted (他还了我一本书, 我寄了一封信给他), so only test 把 + specific object + 交给 / 还给 / 送给 + person against clearly wrong orders.

rules.rule: Turning something into something else, or treating it as something, also needs 把: verb + 成 / 作 must be followed directly by the new form.
rules.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 成 / 作 + New form

examples.zh: 他把这个句子翻译成了中文。
examples.py: tā bǎ zhè ge jù zi fān yì chéng le zhōng wén
examples.en: He translated this sentence into Chinese.

examples.zh: 我一直把他当作好朋友。
examples.py: wǒ yī zhí bǎ tā dàng zuò hǎo péng you
examples.en: I have always thought of him as a good friend.

examples.zh: 对不起，我把十看成了七。
examples.py: duì bu qǐ wǒ bǎ shí kàn chéng le qī
examples.en: Sorry, I misread ten as seven.

rules.note: 当作 and 当成 mean the same here. 把…当作… describes an attitude, so it can be negated with 不 and takes no 了.

rules.rule: A 把 sentence cannot end in a bare verb. If there is no result or direction, add at least 了, a reduplicated verb, or 一下.
rules.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 了 / Verb + 一 + Verb / Verb + 一下

examples.py: nǐ bǎ zhè bēi shuǐ hē le ba
examples.en: Drink this glass of water.

examples.py: wǒ bǎ zhè jiàn shì wàng le
examples.en: I forgot about this.

examples.py: nǐ bǎ zhuō zi cā yī cā
examples.en: Give the table a wipe.

examples.py: qǐng bǎ fáng jiān dǎ sǎo yī xià
examples.en: Please tidy the room up a bit.

rules.note: 了 alone is enough mainly with verbs whose action uses up, removes or loses the object (吃, 喝, 卖, 扔, 丢, 忘, 脱, 关). With other verbs a result is safer: 把作业做完了 rather than 把作业做了, though the short form is heard in casual speech.

rules.rule: Negation goes before 把, not before the verb. Use 没 for something that did not get done (and drop 了); use 别 or 不要 for 'don't'.
rules.pattern: Subject + 没 / 别 / 不要 + 把 + Object + Verb + more

examples.py: wǒ méi bǎ zuò yè dài lái
examples.en: I didn't bring my homework.

examples.py: bié bǎ shǒu jī fàng zài chuáng shàng
examples.en: Don't put your phone on the bed.

examples.py: tā hái méi bǎ qián huán gěi wǒ
examples.en: He still hasn't paid me back.

examples.py: bù yào bǎ zhè jiàn shì gào su tā
examples.en: Don't tell him about this.

rules.note: Plain 不 before 把 is for attitudes, conditions and refusals (他不把我当朋友; 你不把饭吃完，就不能出去玩). A past event that did not happen takes 没把. 把…没 + verb (他把作业没做完) is heard in casual speech but is not the standard order.

rules.rule: Modal verbs and time adverbs also go before 把.
rules.pattern: Subject + 可以 / 要 / 想 / 应该 / 已经 / 马上 + 把 + Object + Verb + more

examples.py: nǐ kě yǐ bǎ chē tíng zài zhè r
examples.en: You can park the car here.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhè běn shū kàn wán
examples.en: I want to finish reading this book.

examples.py: wǒ yǐ jīng bǎ piào mǎi hǎo le
examples.en: I've already bought the tickets.

examples.py: nǐ yīng gāi bǎ yào chī le
examples.en: You should take your medicine.

rules.note: One regular exception: 都 and 全, when they sum up the object, come after it: 我把作业都做完了.

rules.rule: No 把 with verbs that do nothing to the object: 是, 有, 在; liking and knowing (喜欢, 知道, 觉得, 认识); coming and going (来, 去, 到, 回); and seeing or hearing with only 见 / 到 (看见, 听到). Use plain SVO.

examples.py: wǒ hěn xǐ huan zhè ge diàn yǐng
examples.en: I really like this film.

examples.py: wǒ zài lù shàng kàn jiàn tā le
examples.en: I saw him on the way.

examples.py: zhè jiàn shì wǒ zǎo jiù zhī dào le
examples.en: I've known about this for a long time.

examples.py: tā qù nián qù le běi jīng
examples.en: He went to Beijing last year.

rules.note: 看 and 听 do take 把 when a real result follows (我把黑板上的字看清楚了, 把这首歌听完). 忘 is also fine with 把 (把这件事忘了) even though it is a mental verb.

rules.rule: The object of 把 is normally something specific that the listener can identify (这 / 那, 我的, a pronoun, or a bare noun meaning 'the ...'). A new object counted with 一 / 两 / 几 stays after the verb.
rules.pattern: 把 + 这 / 那 / 我的 / bare noun ...   BUT   Verb + Result + 了 + number + measure + Object

examples.py: wǒ bǎ nà běn shū kàn wán le
examples.en: I finished that book.

examples.py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn wán le yī běn shū
examples.en: I finished a book yesterday.

examples.py: tā bǎ kā fēi hē wán le
examples.en: He finished the coffee.

examples.zh: 我在商店买了两件衣服。
examples.py: wǒ zài shāng diàn mǎi le liǎng jiàn yī fu
examples.en: I bought two pieces of clothing at the shop.

rules.note: 一 + measure does occur after 把 when the speaker has one particular thing in mind (我把一件重要的事忘了), and casual speech allows more (我把一杯咖啡喝完了). As a working rule: 'a / some' in English means no 把.

rules.rule: Habits, actions in progress and plain statements with no outcome take ordinary SVO. 把 needs a specific thing and something that happens to it.

examples.py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē kā fēi
examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.py: tā zài fáng jiān lǐ kàn shū
examples.en: He is reading in his room.

examples.py: wǒ hē wán le nà bēi kā fēi
examples.en: I finished that cup of coffee.

examples.py: wǒ bǎ nà bēi kā fēi hē wán le
examples.en: I finished that cup of coffee.

rules.note: With a specific object and a simple result, both orders are correct; 把 puts the attention on what became of the object and is the more usual choice in requests (请把门关上).

rules.rule: 'Can / cannot manage to' complements (verb + 得 / 不 + result) never combine with 把. Keep the object after the verb, or say 能把 / 没把 with a normal result instead.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 / 不 + Result + Object

examples.zh: 我今天做不完这些作业。
examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān zuò bù wán zhè xiē zuò yè
examples.en: I can't finish this homework today.

examples.py: nǐ kàn de dǒng zhè fēng xìn ma
examples.en: Can you understand this letter?

examples.zh: 我今天能把这些作业做完。
examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān néng bǎ zhè xiē zuò yè zuò wán
examples.en: I can get this homework finished today.

right.py: wǒ bǎ zuò yè zuò wán le

contrasts.why: The verb cannot be bare after 把. Say what became of the homework: 做完了.

right.zh: 我把手机放在桌子上了。
right.py: wǒ bǎ shǒu jī fàng zài zhuō zi shàng le
right.en: I put my phone on the table.

contrasts.why: English order 'put the phone on the table' does not work in standard Mandarin: 放 and 在 stay together, so the object moves forward with 把. (放手机在桌子上 is heard in some regional speech.)

contrasts.wrong: 他翻译这个句子成中文了。

right.zh: 他把这个句子翻译成中文了。
right.py: tā bǎ zhè ge jù zi fān yì chéng zhōng wén le
right.en: He translated this sentence into Chinese.

contrasts.why: 翻译成 must be followed straight away by the new form (中文), so the thing translated goes before the verb with 把.

right.py: wǒ méi bǎ zuò yè zuò wán

contrasts.why: 没 goes before 把, not after it, and 了 is dropped after 没. (把作业没做完 is heard in casual speech, but 没把 is the standard order.)

right.py: nǐ kě yǐ bǎ chē tíng zài zhè r
right.en: You can park the car here.

contrasts.why: Modal verbs such as 可以 stand before 把, never between the object and the verb.

right.py: wǒ hěn xǐ huan zhè ge diàn yǐng

contrasts.why: Liking something does nothing to it, so 喜欢 cannot be used with 把.
Seeing someone does not change or move them. 看见 takes its object after the verb.

right.py: wǒ zuò bù wán zhè xiē zuò yè

contrasts.why: 做不完 says the result cannot be reached, and 把 needs a result that is reached. The two never combine.

right.py: qǐng bǎ shū ná chū lái

contrasts.why: The object comes directly after 把; the verb and its direction follow as one block.

cheat: 把 + the thing + verb + what happened to it. Never stop at the bare verb.
放在 / 送到 / 交给 / 翻译成 / 当作 with a specific object: 把 is the standard way.
没, 别, 不要, 可以, 想, 要, 已经 all go BEFORE 把. Didn't happen = 没把, with no 了.
English 'a / some / two ...' object: no 把, plain SVO. 'The / that / my ...': 把 is open.
是, 有, 喜欢, 知道, 觉得, 来, 去, 看见, 听到: no 把.
做不完 / 看得懂 (can or can't manage): no 把.
Nothing happens to the object (habit, ongoing action)? Plain SVO.
